summary: Rodez Cathedral was begun in 1277 after the Romanesque bell tower collapsed, and took roughly 265 years to finish, ending in Flamboyant and early Renaissance work. It has a plain, fortress-like west front and a tall flat-topped bell tower, 87 m high, which the source calls the tallest of its kind in France.

vault_height_m.note: nave height; the first two choir bays have a quadripartite vault also at 30 m

length_interior_m.note: given as 'dans l'oeuvre' (interior); transept width 36.89 m

towers_m.note: bell tower at the north-east angle

phases.what: First stone laid 25 May 1277 by Bishop Raymond de Calmont; work proceeds from east to west
Five radiating chevet chapels about 1320; eleven polygonal choir chapels about 1330
Second campaign: high vault of the first two choir bays, 30 m high, built after 1325
Bell tower built beside the church at the north-east angle; wooden spire contracted in 1386
Transept work from about 1440; choir completed about 1470
Flamboyant nave built from about 1450, slowly 1470-1490, with upper walls under Bernard Anthony after 1503 and first chapels 1520-1540
Bell tower rebuilt after the 1510 fire
Renaissance-style west front designed by Guillaume Philandrier and built by Jean Salvanh (about 1554); pinnacles 1562-1580

events.what: Bell tower of the Romanesque cathedral collapses on 16-17 February.
Fire destroys the wooden spire of the bell tower on 28 April.
Choir fittings removed, tomb of Raymond de Calmont hammered and portal sculptures smashed; tower demolition postponed in early 1794.
Concordat returns the building to Catholic worship.
Lightning strikes the cathedral and damages the organ.
Restoration of the rose window, west front, pinnacles and bell tower, to 1982.
New stained-glass windows by Stéphane Belzère installed, finished November 2006.
